handbookNote: Oklahoma Driver Manual, published by Service Oklahoma (the state agency that took over driver licensing from the Department of Public Safety) -- current official PDF at oklahoma.gov/content/dam/service-oklahoma/Documents/OklahomaDriverManual.pdf, linked from the official written-test and driving-and-automobiles pages on oklahoma.gov/service. The file's own copyright footer reads 'Copyright 2025 Service Oklahoma, State of Oklahoma,' confirming this is the current edition. Note: the task brief pointed to dps.ok.gov as the source, but that domain does not resolve and driver licensing has since moved to Service Oklahoma (oklahoma.gov/service) -- oklahoma.gov/dps.html (the current DPS site) has no driver-manual content at all, confirming the handoff. The full 72-page, 13-chapter text was extracted directly from this PDF via pdftotext and used as the sole grounding source for every question in this bank; no invented facts, no generic driving trivia not actually in the manual. Exam mechanics: confirmed directly from Service Oklahoma's own official written-test FAQ page (oklahoma.gov/service/popular-services/written-test.html) -- the Class D Written Knowledge Test has 20 questions, a passing score of 15 correct (75 percent), and a 60-minute time limit for the online version; two failed online attempts require an in-person retest, with a $4 fee per failed attempt. The manual itself corroborates that the written test is drawn from this manual and covers Oklahoma traffic laws, safe driving practices, and drug/alcohol laws, and states a minimum 1-day wait to retest after failing. Content-depth rationale: the manual is substantive and numerically dense across all 13 chapters -- GDL learner/intermediate stages and restriction codes, license restriction codes B/F/2/4/5/6/7/8/9/0/A/T, REAL ID, the full state speed-limit chart, the 10-point mandatory point system with a per-violation point table, DUI/BAC penalty tiers and Zero Tolerance revocation periods, Move Over/Bernardo-Mills Law, school bus and railroad-crossing right-of-way rules, illegal-parking distance rules, sharing-the-road specifics for pedestrians/bicycles (3-foot passing law)/motorcycles/trucks/trains, and driving-tips chapters covering distracted driving, flood dynamics and crash response -- comfortably supporting a large, non-repetitive bank. 247 questions were written, all traceable to specific manual sections or the official written-test FAQ; several near-templated questions (restriction-code lookups, the state speed-limit chart, Zero Tolerance first/second conviction periods, reckless vs. careless driving point values) were deliberately rephrased with varied wording to avoid false-positive near-duplicate collisions in the build pipeline's Jaccard-similarity dedup, since their underlying facts are genuinely distinct and worth keeping.
